there is a significant trend to earlier use of anti-tumour-necrosis-factor (anti-TNF) therapies in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and less severe disease, and that this has correlated with improvements over time in outcome.
there has been a significant trend towards the earlier use of TNF inhibitors in patients with less-severe disease and that this has correlated with improvements to the treatment outcome.
the use of anti-Tumor Necrosis Factor (anti-TNF) therapies for the treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) has changed over time.

the following: (i) to investigate changes in disease characteristics of patients with RA who started treatment with an anti-TNF therapy in the UK between 2001-2008; (ii) to investigate the effect of these changes on the response to anti-TNF therapy; and (iii) to examine whether there are changes in the drug survival rates over time.

the development of novel anti-TNF agents for the treatment of RA.
